title: Spin-2 propagation requires a new form degree and an infinite Weyl tower

claim.statement: The finite candidate-48 scalar completion cannot be reinterpreted directly as the propagating AdS4 spin-2 system: its adjoint-10 zero-form has the wrong Lorentz branching and form degree, and generic waves require an infinite Weyl-derivative module.
claim.constructiveDirection: Add an SO(2,3)-adjoint one-form connection and a Weyl zero-form tower, treating the existing finite modules only as sources, order parameters, or auxiliary sectors.

representationComparison.spin2Weyl10: chiral rank-4 spinor 5 plus conjugate 5, zero-form curvature

minimalExtension.connection: a = 1/2 δω^{ab} J_ab + ell^{-1} h^a P_a
minimalExtension.curvature: Dbar δω^{ab} + ell^{-2}(ebar^a wedge h^b - ebar^b wedge h^a) = ebar_c wedge ebar_d C^{ab,cd}
minimalExtension.tower: C^{ab,cd} plus all on-shell covariant derivatives

interpretation: Equality of dimensions 10 is not equality of representations: the candidate adjoint and Weyl curvature have incompatible Lorentz content.
Form degree is dynamical data. An adjoint zero-form is a matter/auxiliary module; an adjoint one-form can be a Cartan gauge connection.
Truncating the Weyl tower at a highest level imposes extra derivative constraints and yields finite-type/Killing data rather than generic wave solutions.
The 9-component symmetric-traceless descendant may naturally couple to a metric perturbation, but it is not the 10-component on-shell Weyl curvature.
falsifiers: A direct identification would require an explicit Lorentz intertwiner between 6+4 and Weyl 5+5; none can exist between inequivalent branchings.
A finite propagation claim would require arbitrary functional initial data surviving a finite covariant-constancy chain.
Composite or emergent one-forms remain possible, but must be constructed and shown to transform with the correct inhomogeneous gauge law.
